title: A cluster and its tools
summary: A cluster is a group of machines managed together. kubectl is a command-line tool that asks the Kubernetes API about that cluster.
introduction: A cluster is a group of machines managed together. kubectl is a command-line tool that asks the Kubernetes API about that cluster. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain a cluster and its tools
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A cluster is a group of machines managed together. kubectl is a command-line tool that asks the Kubernetes API about that cluster.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Read these examples without a cluster. To try commands, use only a disposable local learning cluster and the official setup guide. Do not point kubectl at a real organisation's cluster.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Kubernetes. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.
This prints the client version without requiring a working cluster. It does not install a cluster.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why having kubectl is different from having a cluster.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Check the target context before any command that changes resources.
For more detail later, use this [Kubernetes further reading](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/kubernetes-basics/).
